message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.49","text":"And Peter replied, “You have put before us something that can easily be refuted. Nevertheless, hear how God is ignorant of nothing and even foreknows. But first answer me this question of mine: Was the one who wrote the books and said how the world was created and that God does not foreknow a human being or not?” And I said, “A human being.” Peter replied, “Since he was a human being, then, how was it possible for him to know without error how the world was created and that God does not foreknow?”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Εὐκόπως ἐλεγχθῆναι δυνάμενον προέτεινας ἡμῖν","chosen":"You have put before us something that can easily be refuted","rationale":"The substantival neuter participle leaves the object unnamed; “something” preserves that lack of specification rather than supplying “argument.”"},{"source_quote":"οὐδὲν ἀγνοεῖ θεός, ἀλλὰ καὶ προγινώσκει","chosen":"God is ignorant of nothing and even foreknows","rationale":"The rendering preserves the contrast between lacking no knowledge and possessing knowledge in advance; “knows beforehand” is also possible for προγινώσκει."},{"source_quote":"ὃ δὲ πυνθάνομαί σου; πρῶτον ἀπόκριναί μοι.","chosen":"But first answer me this question of mine","rationale":"The relative expression is taken with the following command. The editorial question mark could instead yield the more abrupt “But what I ask you? Answer me first,” but that is less natural English."},{"source_quote":"εἰδέναι ἀψευδῶς","chosen":"to know without error","rationale":"ἀψευδῶς denotes knowing truly or infallibly; “without error” avoids implying merely personal honesty."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.50","text":"And I, already perceiving the solution, said with a slight smile, “Because he was a prophet.” Peter said, “If, then, the prophet, though a human being, was ignorant of nothing because he had received foreknowledge from God, how could the very one who gave a human being the ability to foreknow, being God, have been ignorant?” And I said, “You spoke correctly.” Then Peter said, “Join me, then, in examining this very point further. Since we have agreed that God foreknows everything, it is absolutely necessary that the scriptures which say he is ignorant are false, while those which say he knows are true.” And I said, “It must be so.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αἰσθόμενος ἤδη τὴν ἐπίλυσιν ὑπομειδιῶν","chosen":"already perceiving the solution, said with a slight smile","rationale":"ἐπίλυσις is the solution or resolution of the difficulty, while ὑπομειδιῶν indicates a restrained or slight smile."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὸ ἀπὸ θεοῦ εἰληφέναι τὴν πρόγνωσιν","chosen":"because he had received foreknowledge from God","rationale":"The articular infinitive gives the reason, and πρόγνωσις denotes advance knowledge rather than a prediction uttered by the prophet."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸς ὁ δεδωκὼς ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ προγινώσκειν","chosen":"the very one who gave a human being the ability to foreknow","rationale":"αὐτός emphasizes the giver himself, and the articular infinitive denotes the capacity or act of knowing in advance."},{"source_quote":"Ἔτι οὖν, ἔφη, εἰς αὐτὸ συνδιαπόρησόν μοι","chosen":"Then Peter said, “Join me, then, in examining this very point further”","rationale":"συνδιαπορέω invites joint consideration of a difficulty. “Join me in questioning” is possible, but “examining” is more idiomatic in context."},{"source_quote":"τὰς δὲ γινώσκειν αὐτὸν λεγούσας","chosen":"those which say he knows","rationale":"αὐτόν is construed as the accusative subject of γινώσκειν in contrast with the preceding claim that he is ignorant. Its position also permits the formal alternative “say that someone knows him,” but that leaves the subject unstated and disrupts the explicit contrast."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.51","text":"And Peter said, “If, then, some things in the scriptures are true and others false, our teacher had good reason to say, ‘Become approved money changers,’ since some of the statements in the scriptures are genuine while others are counterfeit. And to those being led astray by the false scriptures, he appropriately revealed the cause of their error by saying, ‘This is why you go astray: you do not know what is true in the scriptures; for this reason you are also ignorant of the power of God.’” And I said, “Very good.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν γραφῶν ἃ μὲν-ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ἃ δὲ ψευδῆ","chosen":"some things in the scriptures are true and others false","rationale":"The neuter forms ἃ and ἀληθῆ are read substantivally of contents or statements within the feminine γραφαί. “Some of the scriptures are true and others false” is contextually possible but would not preserve the printed gender distinction."},{"source_quote":"γίνεσθε τραπεζῖται δόκιμοι","chosen":"Become approved money changers","rationale":"τραπεζῖται are money changers or bankers, and δόκιμοι means tested, approved, or reliable. “Discerning money changers” would express the contextual function but less directly render the adjective."},{"source_quote":"τινῶν μὲν δοκίμων ὄντων λόγων, τινῶν δὲ κιβδήλων","chosen":"some of the statements in the scriptures are genuine while others are counterfeit","rationale":"λόγοι here are statements or passages. δοκίμων and κιβδήλων continue the coin-testing image with genuine versus counterfeit material."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδῶν γραφῶν πλανωμένοις","chosen":"to those being led astray by the false scriptures","rationale":"ἀπό marks the false writings as the source of the error; “because of the false scriptures” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀληθῆ τῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"what is true in the scriptures","rationale":"The neuter substantive denotes the true contents or portions of the writings, not simply acquaintance with the writings as a whole."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὲν-ἐστὶν","issue":"The supplied, image-checked reading prints a hyphen between μὲν and ἐστίν. It appears to be an editorial or typographic separator without semantic force; the translation construes the two printed words separately.","proposed_reading":"μὲν ἐστὶν","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τῶν γραφῶν ἃ μὲν-ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ἃ δὲ ψευδῆ","issue":"If ἃ and ἀληθῆ directly modified the feminine γραφῶν, their neuter gender would be unexpected. They can defensibly be understood substantivally as “some things” or contents among the scriptures, especially in light of the following reference to λόγοι, so no correction is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.52","text":"And Peter replied, “Therefore I have good reason to believe nothing against either God or the righteous people recorded in the law, taking reverent thought as my starting point. For, as I am convinced, Adam was not a transgressor, he who was gestated by the hands of God; nor was Noah a drunkard, he who was found righteous beyond the entire world; nor did Abraham live with three women at once, he who was deemed worthy of many children because of self-control; nor did Jacob have relations with four women, two of whom also happened to be sisters, he who, being the father of twelve tribes, also signaled that the presence of our teacher would come. Moses was not a murderer, and he did not learn to judge from a priest of an idol, he who prophesied God’s law for the entire age and, because of right understanding, was attested as a ‘faithful steward.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οὔτε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πιστεύω οὔτε κατὰ τῶν ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ἀναγραφέντων δικαίων","chosen":"I have good reason to believe nothing against either God or the righteous people recorded in the law","rationale":"With κατά and the genitive, πιστεύω concerns accepting something adverse to the named persons. “Nothing” supplies the object required by natural English without specifying a particular accusation."},{"source_quote":"εὐσεβῶς φρονεῖν προλαμβάνων","chosen":"taking reverent thought as my starting point","rationale":"προλαμβάνων presents reverent judgment as an antecedent presumption or principle. “Presupposing that one should think reverently” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὁ ὑπὸ τῶν τοῦ θεοῦ χειρῶν κυοφορηθείς","chosen":"he who was gestated by the hands of God","rationale":"κυοφορέω ordinarily depicts carrying in the womb or gestation. The deliberately striking image is retained rather than reduced to the more general “formed.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ ὑπὲρ πάντα τὸν κόσμον δίκαιος εὑρεθείς","chosen":"he who was found righteous beyond the entire world","rationale":"ὑπέρ gives a comparative or surpassing sense. “Above the whole world” is more literal, while “more righteous than everyone in the world” makes the comparison explicit."},{"source_quote":"τρισὶν ἅμα συνῄει γυναιξίν","chosen":"live with three women at once","rationale":"σύνειμι with the dative can mean associate or cohabit and may carry a sexual or marital implication here. “Have relations with” is a possible stronger rendering."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε Ἰακὼβ τετράσιν ἐκοινώνει","chosen":"nor did Jacob have relations with four women","rationale":"κοινωνέω can mean share or associate with and, in this marital context, have relations with. “Women” is supplied from the preceding clause and confirmed by the feminine relative ὧν and ἀδελφαί."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ διδασκάλου ἡμῶν παρουσίαν ἐσήμανεν ἐλθεῖν","chosen":"signaled that the presence of our teacher would come","rationale":"παρουσία is retained as “presence,” while ἐλθεῖν separately expresses its coming; translating only “the coming of our teacher” would collapse the source’s wording."},{"source_quote":"οὐ Μωϋσῆς φονεὺς ἦν, καὶ παρὰ ἱερέως εἰδώλου κρίνειν ἐμάνθανεν","chosen":"Moses was not a murderer, and he did not learn to judge from a priest of an idol","rationale":"The single οὐ is taken as governing both coordinated allegations, as required by the surrounding sequence of denials. A formally possible reading that affirms the second predicate would conflict with that structure."},{"source_quote":"παντὶ τῷ αἰῶνι τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ νόμον προφητεύσας","chosen":"prophesied God’s law for the entire age","rationale":"The dative is read temporally or as indicating the age for which the prophecy was given. “To the entire age” and, if αἰών is spatially extended, “to the whole world” are possible alternatives."},{"source_quote":"πιστὸς οἰκονόμος","chosen":"faithful steward","rationale":"οἰκονόμος denotes one entrusted with managing a household or its affairs; “manager” is a possible modern alternative."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
